text: The Flåm Railway was the highlight of our year. Every turn showed a new waterfall.
Bergen is charming and the hotel breakfast was excellent. The Fløibanen view at sunset was perfect.
We saw the northern lights on two of three evenings. Freezing cold, but the guides gave us warm suits.
Reine looked unreal. Sleeping in a red fishermen's cabin was a dream come true.
Great food walk in Grünerløkka. The jazz bar was a bit crowded but fun.
The Seven Sisters waterfall from the boat, then the hike to Skageflå. Worth every krone.
The fjord cruise was breathtaking, but the bus to Flam was late and crowded.
Total silence, home-cooked meals and long light evenings in Jotunheimen. Exactly the quiet trip we wanted.
Very hard hike, eleven hours for us, but our guide Ingrid kept everyone safe. The view is famous for a reason.
We saw walruses and a polar bear far away from the boat. Pyramiden felt like a time machine.
Easy and well organised. All the tickets worked and the views from the train were stunning.
Preikestolen in the morning mist was magical, and the Lysefjord cruise showed it from below.
Driving my own husky team across Finnmark was the best thing I have ever done. The lavvu night was cosy.
It rained all three days and the walking tour of Bryggen was cancelled. The hotel was fine.
Cloudy every night, so no aurora at all. The whale watching was nice, but we came for the lights.
Our guide Lars knew everything about the Nærøyfjord. Small group, calm pace, lovely hotels.
Stunning beaches at Haukland. The kayak trip was cold but amazing. Dinner prices in Lofoten are high.
Best city trip ever. The National Museum, the opera house roof and so much good coffee.
Beautiful fjord, but two big cruise ships arrived at the same time and Geiranger village was packed.
Wonderful nature and kind hosts. The bus from Oslo took longer than expected.
Too hard for me. The trip description says hard, and they mean it. My knees still hurt.
Incredible landscapes around Longyearbyen. Very expensive, but nothing compares to the high Arctic.
Nice route, but the winter timetable meant long waits in Myrdal.
Good hike, clear instructions and a friendly guide. Stavanger old town is small but pretty.
Amazing dogs and great food at the lodge in Alta. Bring more warm socks than you think.
The fish market, Bryggen and Mount Fløyen in one weekend. The Bergen Card saved us a lot of money.
Lovely trip, though the train from Bergen to Myrdal was full in July. Book seats early.
Green and purple lights dancing over the Lyngen Alps. I cried a little. Thank you Fjord Trips.
Midnight sun on the beach at Uttakleiv. The Reinebringen hike was steep but the guide was patient.
The food tastings were great but the hotel room was very small and noisy on Friday night.
Ålesund's art nouveau town and the Geirangerfjord in one trip. Very well planned.
We saw reindeer near the lake on day two. A perfect escape from city life.
Amazing nature, but the boat expedition was shortened because of sea ice. We got a partial refund.
Two days, train, boat and bus, and we saw the best of western Norway. Stalheimskleiva is unforgettable.
Pulpit Rock was so crowded we had to queue for a photo. Go early if you can.
Northern lights from the lavvu tent on our last night. Small group of six, perfect guides.
Good value, central hotel and a nice guided walk. Restaurants in Bergen are expensive.
Our booking confirmation had the wrong date and nobody answered the phone for two days. Very disappointing.
Tromsø is a fun little city. Two clear nights out of three. The minibus was comfortable.
The scenery is ten out of ten, the weather was three out of ten. Bring rain gear.
The guided food walk was the best part. Try the cinnamon buns. Oslo is pricey but lovely.
Great views from Ørnesvingen. The Skageflå hike is steep at the start, then easy.
Hardest and best day of my life. Start at 6 am like the guide says and you will beat the crowds.
Glaciers calving into the sea in front of us. The armed guide made us feel safe the whole time.
Easy self-guided trip. The night in Flåm was quiet and the breakfast was good.
Clear blue sky, Pulpit Rock, then shrimp by the harbour in Stavanger. Perfect three days.
Fantastic huskies, but minus 28 degrees was too cold for me. The lodge was warm and friendly.
Beautiful cabin, but no mobile signal at all. Great for some people, hard for others.
Bryggen at night is beautiful. We loved the colourful houses and the friendly people.
Flåm, the Nærøyfjord and Bergen in four relaxed days. My parents (both over 70) managed everything easily.
